title.wall_note: No wall-thickness callout on the sheet; columns lettered 230x375 mm

assumptions: The drawing could only be read at reduced resolution (1413 x 2000 out of the file's 9356 x 13245) because no image-cropping / zoom tool was available in this session. Fine detail — door swing arcs, the exact extent of window symbols, and the individual stair treads — is at the limit of legibility, so every 'pos' and 'width' below that is not backed by a written figure is a measurement against the 7620 and 15441 overall dimensions, at 8.38 mm per rendered pixel.

The sheet carries NO door/window schedule. Every height_mm, sill_mm and lintel_mm given is a standard value (windows 1200 h / 900 sill, ventilator 600 h / 1800 sill, doors 2100 h), NOT read from the sheet.

The sheet carries NO wall-thickness callout. Thicknesses are inferred: 9" (230 mm) for the compound / external walls and for the two spine walls and the wall line that carry the 230x375 columns; 4.5" (115 mm) for the toilet, dress and lawn-2 partitions. The only thickness actually written anywhere on the sheet is the 230x375 of the columns.

The written clear room sizes over-sum the written overall width of 7620 by roughly 200-350 mm across the middle band (LAWN-2 1400 + KITCHEN 2200 + FOYER 1445 + TOILET-2 2000 + partitions). The centre-line grid was therefore laid on the drawn geometry, measured against the 7620 / 15441 overalls, and the written clear sizes are carried unchanged in each room's size_label.

W4 (BED ROOM-1 north wall, onto LAWN-1) is the one window whose extent I could read directly off the drawing: the wall is broken from x 2.04 to x 11.00 ft, i.e. about 2730 mm. This is unusually wide for a window but it is what is drawn, and the W4 mark sits centred in that break.

W1 and W2 widths could not be resolved. Both are placed centred on their marks in the DINING/LIVING south wall and given a 1500 mm width. W3 is likewise placed centred on its mark, 1000 mm wide, onto LAWN-2. W5 is placed centred on its mark in the spine wall onto LAWN-1 and given 1200 mm, which is the largest that fits the 1512 mm length of wall available between the LAWN-1 wall and the north wall.
V1 is the only opening whose gap I could read cleanly at both jambs: the TOILET-2 south wall is broken from x 20.68 to 23.10 ft (about 740 mm) with the V1 mark centred in it.

NO ENTRANCE DOOR is discernible in the house's south wall between the Main Gate and the STAIRCASE, and none has been invented. The C2 and C3 column label boxes overlie that stretch of wall in the render, so an entrance door may be hidden beneath them. As traced, the house has no external door.

STAIRCASE: read as a U (dog-leg) — the 2121 mm wide shaft is split down the middle by a well line into two flights that match the written W=1000, and the treads are drawn horizontally so the flights climb in y. About 12 tread lines were counted per flight over the drawn depth, which with the written T=275 plus a 1000 landing fills the 13.86 ft shaft. The LANDING POSITION could not be resolved; I have taken it at the south (bottom) end, with the ascent starting at the north end beside door D, because that is the end the FOYER door enters at. The alternative reading (landing at the north end) cannot be ruled out at this resolution. 12 treads x 2 flights at R=150 implies a floor-to-floor of about 3750 mm, which is higher than usual — the tread count may be 10 per flight.

No wall is drawn across the head of the stair between C6 and C7 on the y=20.35 line, so none is listed there — the stair mouth is open to the FOYER lobby. C7 stands free on that line rather than in a wall.

The mark 'Opening 2' is used twice at two different drawn widths — 5.26 ft between BED ROOM-1 and DRESS-1, and 4.29 ft between the FOYER and DINING/LIVING. Both are reported as measured rather than forced to one size, since there is no schedule to rule on it.

A short double-line segment appears in TOILET-1's south wall at roughly x 2.3 to 7.1 ft, facing LAWN-2. It carries no mark and I could not tell at this resolution whether it is a window symbol or simply the wall drawn in two lines, so it has NOT been listed as an opening. TOILET-1 therefore has no window in this model.

Three doors are marked 'D' and three 'D1'; both marks are copied exactly as written and left un-numbered. All six are single doors — the drawn gaps are 750-900 mm and no two-leaf symbol appears anywhere on the sheet.
C3 is drawn about 0.8 ft lower than C1 and C2 in the render; I have aligned all three to the y=6.49 wall line on the assumption that the offset is a label-box artefact.

FRONT LAWN is written 5390X1270 but is drawn about 5390 x 1860 between the house wall and the compound wall. The room box follows the drawn extent; the written figure is kept in size_label. The strip between the FRONT LAWN and the Main Gate (x 18.06 to 24.62) is unlabelled on the sheet and has been left as no room rather than given an invented name.
The north arrow is drawn tilted up and to the right at roughly 40-45 degrees from horizontal; north_deg is given as 45, measured off the compass symbol.

plan_name 'GROUND FLOOR PLAN' is NOT written on the sheet — it is inferred from the presence of the Main Gate, the front lawn and an up-going staircase. No project name, revision or date appears anywhere on the drawing.
